newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates lower on loosening liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates lower on loosening liquidity.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates were lower at midday on Wednesday as liquidity gradually returned to the banking system after the Chinese new year holiday which ended on Monday, dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate was at 6.099 percent against Tuesday's 6.260 close, with 30-day commercial paper falling to 5.70-5.75 from 5.75-6.00.
But dealers said they did not expect any sharp rate fall as the market's accumulated reserve excess still showed a negative T$585.8 billion.
The rates had been at yearly high levels due to business funding needs before the five-day Chinese new year holiday, but they fell sharply on Tuesday after cash demand eased.
Government bond yields were higher on profit-taking triggered by worries over likely hikes in water fees and oil product prices, dealers said.
The 10-year 86/4 bond yield was at 6.0550-6.0650 percent against 6.0480-6.0490.
